findings.claim_ground: src/urban_network_analysis/Engines/_metric_reuse_scratch.py:542 ('job': dict(job) — shallow) with src/urban_network_analysis/batch/cohort.py:472-478,499-501,534-537 (the same caller-owned d_weights/knn_weights objects flow into the store)
findings.description: Latent staleness hazard: the store's internal binding lease aliases caller-owned MUTABLE arrays. register() copies the four output arrays (immutable private copies) but only shallow-copies the job dict, so job['d_weights']/['knn_weights'] reference the caller's arrays. If a caller mutates a previously-passed array in place, later SPLIT sourcing compares against the mutated bytes while the stored outputs hold pre-mutation bits, and a wrong (stale) serve results — demonstrated live in a synthetic frame (served==stale True, served==truth False; bundle mode is NOT exposed because MetricID v2 hashes current bytes). Not manifested anywhere in-repo: batch workers build fresh UNA/Settings/inputs per row and no caller mutates passed arrays. Tension to record: designs/04 step 2 says 'Keep fields in immutable internal storage' — the reused output fields are immutable, the agreement-binding lease is not. Suggested disposition: copy the two binding arrays inside register() (mirroring the outputs) or document the no-post-call-mutation caller contract in the store docstring; neither is required for the current committed callers.
findings.evidence: probe check 'HAZARD: split serves stale pre-mutation bits | served==stale(True) served==truth(False)' and 'registered job aliases caller array ... is W1' (this session's console custody)
